name: Oregon

localAgencies.name: Lane Regional Air Protection Agency (LRAPA)
localAgencies.notes: Permitting authority for PSD, minor NSR, nonattainment NSR, and Title V in Lane County (per EPA).

overview: Oregon DEQ issues Air Contaminant Discharge Permits (ACDPs) for minor sources and for new major sources/major modifications, plus Title V operating permits for major sources. Which ACDP applies depends on the source category in the Table of Activities and Sources (OAR 340-216-8010, Table 1): Part A sources qualify for a Basic ACDP, Part B for a General, Simple, or Standard ACDP, and Part C must get a Standard ACDP. Permits carry Plant Site Emission Limits (PSELs) compared against Significant Emission Rates (SERs). Many sources need a Notice of Construction even without a permit (OAR Division 210), and every permit needs a Land Use Compatibility Statement. Cleaner Air Oregon adds facility risk assessment for toxic air contaminants. LRAPA permits in Lane County; EPA Region 10 permits in Indian Country and on the Outer Continental Shelf.

permitTypes.name: Notice of Construction / Notice of Intent to Construct
permitTypes.description: Many sources must submit a Notice of Construction even if no permit is required; sources that believe no permit is needed submit an AQ104 Notice of Intent to Construct.

permitTypes.name: Basic ACDP
permitTypes.description: Contains only the most significant rules for listed Part A source categories; no PSEL; term up to 10 years. Categories: autobody shops (Portland area), concrete manufacturing, crematories, gas-fired boilers, prepared feeds, rock crushers, surface coating, and other sources taking enforceable limits.
permitTypes.thresholds: Typical actual emissions under 10 tons/yr (DEQ ACDP application instructions comparison table).

permitTypes.name: General ACDPs
permitTypes.description: Issued by order for a source category, up to 10 years; sources are assigned if they qualify and actual emissions stay below the General ACDP PSELs. Categories include degreasers (GP 05), dry cleaners (06), asphalt plants (07), rock crushers (08), concrete (09), sawmills (10), boilers (11), crematories (12), grain elevators (13), prepared feeds (14), seed cleaning (15), coffee roasters (16), bulk gasoline plants (17), electric power generators (18), clay ceramics (19), hospital sterilizers (20), gasoline dispensing (22, 23), metal fabrication/finishing (25, 29), plating and polishing (26), surface coating (27), air curtain incinerators (31), and emergency engines (Attachment 32a).

permitTypes.name: Simple ACDP
permitTypes.description: For Part B sources with source-specific PSELs below the SERs; term up to 10 years. A source may request a Standard ACDP instead to keep a netting basis.

permitTypes.name: Standard ACDP
permitTypes.description: For Part C sources, sources requesting a PSEL at or above the SER, sources keeping a netting basis, and sources meeting potential-to-emit criteria; term up to 5 years. Also used for NSR/PSD sources.
permitTypes.quote: the potential to emit 100 tons or more of any regulated pollutant, except GHG, in a year

permitTypes.name: Construction ACDP
permitTypes.description: Covers Type 3 or Type 4 construction or modification changes (OAR 340-210-0225) for sources needing a Standard ACDP or Title V permit. Optional for ACDP sources, required for Title V sources. Does not authorize operation.

permitTypes.name: Major New Source Review (PSD and nonattainment/maintenance area NSR)
permitTypes.description: New major sources and major modifications obtain a Standard ACDP (DEQ lists a separate initial fee for NSR/PSD Standard ACDPs). Oregon's major NSR rules are in OAR Division 224.

permitTypes.name: Oregon Title V Operating Permit
permitTypes.description: For major sources; about 120 sources are permitted. Sources can take federally enforceable limits to remain synthetic minors in the ACDP program. Funded by emission, base, and user fees (OAR Division 220).
permitTypes.thresholds: Potential to emit 100 tons of any criteria pollutant, 10 tons of any single HAP, or 25 tons of any combination of HAPs (restated from DEQ's Title V Rules and Fees page).

oilAndGas.summary: Oregon has no oil production; DEQ's General and Basic ACDP lists include no oil and gas production permits. Related categories are bulk gasoline plants (GP 17), gasoline dispensing (GP 22/23), and gas-fired boilers (Basic 04, GP 11).
